features.name: non_industry_sponsor_proxy
features.description: Maximum of academic and government sponsorship indicators to serve as a proxy for non-commercial funding.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a strong negative margin indicator for the SVM by explicitly combining known non-commercial sponsorship types.

features.name: global_scale_index
features.description: Normalized index combining the number of countries and international trial status.
features.expected_model_benefit: Smooth continuous feature that helps the linear model separate large-scale global trials from localized ones.

features.name: trial_rigor_score
features.description: Composite score of randomization, blinding, and evidence strength.
features.expected_model_benefit: Aggregates binary and continuous rigor metrics into a single linear projection, reducing sparsity.

features.name: ai_tech_intensity
features.description: Average of positive mentions for machine learning, deep learning, AI, and algorithms.
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates a continuous severity measure of AI focus, which is more effective for SVM margins than individual sparse binary flags.

features.name: digital_health_focus
features.description: Maximum indicator across software, mobile app, and wearable mentions.
features.expected_model_benefit: Groups related digital health modalities into a single feature, providing a cleaner signal for the linear model.

features.name: enrollment_phase_interaction
features.description: Interaction term between enrollment size and trial phase, normalized to [0, 1].
features.expected_model_benefit: Allows the linear SVM to capture the non-linear relationship where late-phase, large-enrollment trials behave differently than others.

features.name: vulnerable_pop_inclusion
features.description: Indicates if the trial includes either children or older adults.
features.expected_model_benefit: Consolidates age-related inclusion criteria into a single dimension, simplifying the feature space.

features.name: ai_risk_awareness
features.description: Maximum indicator across bias, safety, and privacy mentions.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a unified measure of risk consideration, which may correlate with institutional backing and resources.

features.name: deployment_evidence_ratio
features.description: Ratio of real-world deployment score to evidence strength score, with a small constant to prevent division by zero.
features.expected_model_benefit: Highlights trials that are highly deployed but have lower formal evidence, a pattern that may separate different types of sponsors.

features.name: commercial_viability_judgment
features.description: Semantic assessment of the trial's description and AI use type to determine its potential for commercialization and profit, scoring from 0.0 (purely academic/basic research) to 10.0 (highly commercial product).
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a nuanced, continuous measure of commercial intent that raw keywords might miss, aligning well with the linear model's need for smooth gradients.

features.name: regulatory_complexity_judgment
features.description: Evaluates the complexity of the trial's regulatory pathway based on disease area, phase, and AI technology used, scored from 0.0 (low burden) to 5.0 (high burden).
features.expected_model_benefit: High regulatory burden often requires significant funding. This semantic score gives the SVM a proxy for required capital.

features.name: innovation_novelty_judgment
features.description: Assesses the novelty of the AI application within the specified disease area, from 0.0 (standard/routine) to 1.0 (highly novel/experimental).
features.expected_model_benefit: Differentiates between cutting-edge research and mature applications, providing a continuous feature that helps separate funding sources.
